---@group 表现
---@var IdleFlapSpeed:number=0.55
---@name 待机扇翅频率
---@desc 未被骑乘时每秒轻扇翅膀的次数
---@group 表现
---@end

local UnityEngine = CS.UnityEngine
local Vector2 = CS.UnityEngine.Vector2
local Vector3 = CS.UnityEngine.Vector3
local Quaternion = CS.UnityEngine.Quaternion
local Mathf = CS.UnityEngine.Mathf
local Time = CS.UnityEngine.Time
local Input = CS.UnityEngine.Input
local KeyCode = CS.UnityEngine.KeyCode
local DouyinInputService = CS.DouyinInputService
local DouyinUIService = CS.DouyinUIService
local UIType = CS.UIType
local EventTrigger = CS.UnityEngine.EventSystems.EventTrigger
local EventTriggerType = CS.UnityEngine.EventSystems.EventTriggerType
local RuntimeScope = require("official.core.runtime_scope")

local runtimeScope = RuntimeScope.from(self)

local deadZone = 0.12
local idleDamping = 4.5
local horizontalAccel = 9
local verticalAccel = 7
local pitchAngle = 18
local rollAngle = 20
local motionLerpSpeed = 5
local flightFlapAmplitude = 30
local idleFlapAmplitude = 8
local bobAmplitude = 0.035

local rb = nil
local visualRoot = nil
local wingLeft = nil
local wingRight = nil
local neckRoot = nil
local tailNodes = {}
local tailBaseX = {-10.3, -6.9, -3.4, 1.1, 8.0, 14.9, 21.8, 26.4}

local moveVec = Vector2.zero
local onMoveInputStart = nil
local onMoveInputPerform = nil
local onMoveInputCancel = nil

local riderActive = false
local occupied = false
local controlReady = false
local controlSupported = false
local controlPending = false
local nextControlTry = 0
local velocityX = 0
local velocityY = 0
local velocityZ = 0
local m_yaw = 0
local m_pitch = 0
local m_roll = 0
local animationTime = 0
local rideCameraApplied = false

local ascendBtn = nil
local ascendTrigger = nil
local descendBtn = nil
local descendTrigger = nil
local btnAscend = false
local btnDescend = false

local function clearTrigger(trigger)
  if trigger == nil then return end
  if trigger.triggers ~= nil then
    trigger.triggers:Clear()
  end
end

local function bindTrigger(btn, onDown, onUp)
  if btn == nil or btn.gameObject == nil then return nil end
  local trigger = btn.gameObject:GetComponent(typeof(EventTrigger))
  if trigger == nil then
    trigger = btn.gameObject:AddComponent(typeof(EventTrigger))
  end
  clearTrigger(trigger)

  local entryDown = EventTrigger.Entry()
  entryDown.eventID = EventTriggerType.PointerDown
  entryDown.callback:AddListener(function(_) onDown() end)
  trigger.triggers:Add(entryDown)

  local entryUp = EventTrigger.Entry()
  entryUp.eventID = EventTriggerType.PointerUp
  entryUp.callback:AddListener(function(_) onUp() end)
  trigger.triggers:Add(entryUp)

  return trigger
end

local function setButtonText(btn, text)
  if btn == nil then return end
  local label = btn:GetComponentInChildren(typeof(CS.UnityEngine.UI.Text), true)
  if label ~= nil then
    label.gameObject:SetActive(true)
    label.text = text
  end
end

local function setupActionButton(uiType, btnText, onDown, onUp)
  local btn = DouyinUIService.GetInteractionButton(uiType)
  if btn == nil then return nil, nil end
  btn.gameObject:SetActive(true)
  btn.transition = CS.UnityEngine.UI.Selectable.Transition.None
  local tween = btn.gameObject:GetComponentInChildren(typeof(CS.ButtonTweenEffect), true)
  if tween ~= nil then
    tween.enabled = false
  end
  setButtonText(btn, btnText)
  local trigger = bindTrigger(btn, onDown, onUp)
  return btn, trigger
end

local function hideButton(btn, trigger)
  if trigger ~= nil then clearTrigger(trigger) end
  if btn ~= nil then btn.gameObject:SetActive(false) end
end

local function showFlightButtons()
  if ascendBtn ~= nil or descendBtn ~= nil then return end
  ascendBtn, ascendTrigger = setupActionButton(
    UIType.CustomMain, "上升",
    function() if riderActive then btnAscend = true end end,
    function() btnAscend = false end
  )
  descendBtn, descendTrigger = setupActionButton(
    UIType.CustomSub, "下降",
    function() if riderActive then btnDescend = true end end,
    function() btnDescend = false end
  )
end

local function hideFlightButtons()
  hideButton(ascendBtn, ascendTrigger)
  ascendBtn = nil
  ascendTrigger = nil
  hideButton(descendBtn, descendTrigger)
  descendBtn = nil
  descendTrigger = nil
  btnAscend = false
  btnDescend = false
end

local function applyRideCamera()
  if rideCameraApplied then return end
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetDistance(11)
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetPitch(16)
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetOffset(Vector3(0, 1.9, 0))
  rideCameraApplied = true
end

local function restoreRideCamera()
  if not rideCameraApplied then return end
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetDistance(4)
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetPitch(0)
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetOffset(Vector3(0, 0, 0))
  rideCameraApplied = false
end

local function clearInput()
  moveVec = Vector2.zero
  btnAscend = false
  btnDescend = false
  velocityX = 0
  velocityY = 0
  velocityZ = 0
end

local function requestControl()
  if not controlSupported or controlPending or controlReady then return end
  if self:IsNull() then return end
  if self:HasControllership() then
    controlReady = true
    return
  end

  controlPending = true
  self:RequestControllership(function(success)
    controlPending = false
    if self:IsNull() then return end
    if success and self:HasControllership() then
      controlReady = true
    else
      nextControlTry = Time.time + 1.0
    end
  end)
end

local function releaseControl()
  controlReady = false
  if controlSupported and self:HasControllership() then
    self:ReleaseControllership()
  end
end

local function resolveVerticalInput()
  local up = Input.GetKey(KeyCode.E) or btnAscend
  local down = Input.GetKey(KeyCode.Q) or btnDescend
  if up and not down then return 1 end
  if down and not up then return -1 end
  return 0
end

local function findNodes()
  if runtimeScope == nil then return end
  visualRoot = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot")
  wingLeft = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot/WingLeftRoot")
  wingRight = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot/WingRightRoot")
  neckRoot = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot/NeckRoot")

  tailNodes[1] = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot/TailRoot")
  local path = "DragonRoot/VisualRoot/TailRoot"
  for index = 1, 7 do
    path = path .. string.format("/Tail%02d", index)
    tailNodes[index + 1] = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath(path)
  end
end

local function animateCreature()
  animationTime = animationTime + Time.deltaTime
  local flying = occupied
  local flapHz = flying and FlightFlapSpeed or IdleFlapSpeed
  local flapAmplitude = flying and flightFlapAmplitude or idleFlapAmplitude
  local flap = Mathf.Sin(animationTime * flapHz * 2 * Mathf.PI) * flapAmplitude

  -- Unity 的 X 轴相对 glTF 镜像：左翼位于 -X，需要反向 Z 旋转抬翼。
  if wingLeft ~= nil then
    wingLeft.localEulerAngles = Vector3(0, 0, -flap)
  end
  if wingRight ~= nil then
    wingRight.localEulerAngles = Vector3(0, 0, flap)
  end

  local swayAmplitude = flying and 5.0 or 2.5
  for index = 1, #tailNodes do
    local node = tailNodes[index]
    if node ~= nil then
      local sway = Mathf.Sin(animationTime * 1.25 - index * 0.42) * swayAmplitude
      node.localEulerAngles = Vector3(tailBaseX[index], sway, 0)
    end
  end

  if neckRoot ~= nil then
    local neckBob = Mathf.Sin(animationTime * 0.85) * 1.2
    neckRoot.localEulerAngles = Vector3(neckBob, 0, 0)
  end

  if visualRoot ~= nil then
    local bob = 0
    if flying then
      bob = Mathf.Sin(animationTime * 2.1) * bobAmplitude
    end
    visualRoot.localPosition = Vector3(0, bob, 0)
  end
end

function Start()
  rb = self.gameObject:GetComponent(typeof(UnityEngine.Rigidbody))
  controlSupported = self.HasControllership ~= nil and self.RequestControllership ~= nil
  findNodes()

  onMoveInputStart = function()
    -- 起手时保持当前方向，由 Perform 覆盖。
  end
  onMoveInputPerform = function(vec)
    moveVec = vec
  end
  onMoveInputCancel = function()
    moveVec = Vector2.zero
  end

  DouyinInputService.onMoveInputStart:AddListener(onMoveInputStart)
  DouyinInputService.onMoveInputPerform:AddListener(onMoveInputPerform)
  DouyinInputService.onMoveInputCancel:AddListener(onMoveInputCancel)
end

function SetOccupied(value)
  occupied = value == true
end

function SetRiderActive(active)
  if active then
    if riderActive then return end
    riderActive = true
    occupied = true
    velocityX = 0
    velocityY = 0
    velocityZ = 0
    m_pitch = 0
    m_roll = 0
    m_yaw = self.transform.eulerAngles.y
    controlReady = not controlSupported
    nextControlTry = 0
    applyRideCamera()
    showFlightButtons()
    if controlSupported then
      requestControl()
    end
  else
    if not riderActive then return end
    riderActive = false
    occupied = false
    clearInput()
    m_pitch = 0
    m_roll = 0
    hideFlightButtons()
    restoreRideCamera()
    releaseControl()
  end
end

function OnControllershipTransferred(prevPlayer, currentPlayer)
  if not controlSupported then return end
  controlReady = self:HasControllership()
  if not controlReady and riderActive then
    nextControlTry = Time.time + 1.0
  end
end

function Update()
  animateCreature()

  if riderActive and controlSupported and not controlReady and not controlPending
    and Time.time >= nextControlTry then
    requestControl()
  end
end

function FixedUpdate()
  if not riderActive or not controlReady or rb == nil then return end

  local dt = Time.fixedDeltaTime
  local forwardInput = moveVec.y
  local turnInput = moveVec.x
  if math.abs(forwardInput) < deadZone then forwardInput = 0 end
  if math.abs(turnInput) < deadZone then turnInput = 0 end
  local verticalInput = resolveVerticalInput()

  m_yaw = m_yaw + turnInput * TurnSpeed * dt
  local targetPitch = -verticalInput * pitchAngle
  local targetRoll = -turnInput * rollAngle
  local lerpT = Mathf.Clamp01(motionLerpSpeed * dt)
  m_pitch = Mathf.Lerp(m_pitch, targetPitch, lerpT)
  m_roll = Mathf.Lerp(m_roll, targetRoll, lerpT)
  rb:MoveRotation(Quaternion.Euler(m_pitch, m_yaw, m_roll))

  local forward = self.transform.forward
  local horizontalForward = Vector3(forward.x, 0, forward.z)
  if horizontalForward.sqrMagnitude <= 0.0001 then
    horizontalForward = Vector3(0, 0, 1)
  else
    horizontalForward:Normalize()
  end

  local targetX = horizontalForward.x * forwardInput * HorizontalSpeed
  local targetZ = horizontalForward.z * forwardInput * HorizontalSpeed
  local targetY = verticalInput * VerticalSpeed
  local horizontalStep = (forwardInput == 0 and idleDamping or horizontalAccel) * dt
  local verticalStep = (verticalInput == 0 and idleDamping or verticalAccel) * dt

  velocityX = Mathf.MoveTowards(velocityX, targetX, horizontalStep)
  velocityZ = Mathf.MoveTowards(velocityZ, targetZ, horizontalStep)
  velocityY = Mathf.MoveTowards(velocityY, targetY, verticalStep)

  local nextPosition = rb.position + Vector3(velocityX, velocityY, velocityZ) * dt
  rb:MovePosition(nextPosition)
end

import bpy
import math
from mathutils import Vector

GLB = "/Users/a1234/Library/Application Support/AI World Creator/projects/project_lapv8fm0/ai-sessions/workspace_i6ox5xen/assets/module/module-black-dragon/package/model.glb"

bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=GLB)

# World: neutral dark gray so a black dragon still reveals form.
world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World")
world.use_nodes = True
bg = world.node_tree.nodes["Background"]
bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.055, 0.06, 0.07, 1.0)
bg.inputs[1].default_value = 1.0
bpy.context.scene.world = world

# Bounds
mins = Vector((1e9, 1e9, 1e9))
maxs = Vector((-1e9, -1e9, -1e9))
for obj in bpy.context.scene.objects:
    if obj.type != 'MESH':
        continue
    for corner in obj.bound_box:
        p = obj.matrix_world @ Vector(corner)
        mins.x = min(mins.x, p.x); mins.y = min(mins.y, p.y); mins.z = min(mins.z, p.z)
        maxs.x = max(maxs.x, p.x); maxs.y = max(maxs.y, p.y); maxs.z = max(maxs.z, p.z)
center = (mins + maxs) * 0.5
print("BOUNDS", tuple(mins), tuple(maxs), "CENTER", tuple(center))

# Ground
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=40, location=(center.x, center.y, mins.z - 0.01))
ground = bpy.context.object
ground.name = "Ground"
mat = bpy.data.materials.new("GroundMat")
mat.use_nodes = True
bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (0.12, 0.125, 0.13, 1.0)
bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.85
ground.data.materials.append(mat)

# Lights
def add_area(name, loc, energy, size, color):
    data = bpy.data.lights.new(name, 'AREA')
    data.energy = energy
    data.shape = 'DISK'
    data.size = size
    data.color = color
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, data)
    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(obj)
    obj.location = loc
    d = center - obj.location
    obj.rotation_euler = d.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y').to_euler()
    return obj

add_area("Key", center + Vector((7.0, -7.0, 8.0)), 1600, 7.0, (1.0, 0.96, 0.90))
add_area("Fill", center + Vector((-8.0, -5.0, 4.5)), 900, 8.0, (0.62, 0.74, 1.0))
add_area("Rim", center + Vector((0.0, 9.0, 7.0)), 1400, 6.0, (1.0, 0.86, 0.70))
add_area("Top", center + Vector((0.0, 0.0, 11.0)), 600, 9.0, (1.0, 1.0, 1.0))

# Camera
cam_data = bpy.data.cameras.new("Camera")
cam_data.lens = 55
cam = bpy.data.objects.new("Camera", cam_data)
bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(cam)
bpy.context.scene.camera = cam

scene = bpy.context.scene
scene.render.engine = 'BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT'
scene.eevee.taa_render_samples = 48
scene.render.resolution_x = 900
scene.render.resolution_y = 900
scene.render.film_transparent = False
scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'AgX'
scene.view_settings.look = 'AgX - Medium High Contrast'
scene.view_settings.exposure = 1.15

target = Vector((center.x, center.y + 0.15, center.z + 0.05))

def render_view(name, cam_pos):
    cam.location = Vector(cam_pos)
    direction = target - cam.location
    cam.rotation_euler = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y').to_euler()
    scene.render.filepath = f"{OUT}/{name}.png"
    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)

# glTF +Z (front) imports as Blender -Y.

render_view("side", (10.8, 1.2, 2.4))
render_view("front", (0.0, -11.0, 2.2))

print("DONE")

parts.text: Now read the images.

Now I can see. It looks like a cute chibi dragon/bat, not the sleek, imposing western dragon in the reference. Problems:
- Body is a lumpy pear-shaped mass; legs are cylindrical tubes, straight and stiff; reference has muscular, sculpted limbs with defined shoulders/thighs.
- Wings are flat, upright leaf shapes with spars; reference has large arched bat wings with long finger bones and deep scalloped membrane, sweeping upward and outward.
- Neck is too short and thick; reference has a long, elegant S-curved neck.
- Head is too big/cartoony with a blunt snout and horns that look like spikes; reference has a narrow, elongated skull with swept-back horns and a pronounced jaw.
- Tail is a thick cylinder extending backward, droops and lies low; reference has a long tail that curves up and ends at shoulder height with a large blade.
- Proportions: belly too round, shoulders not defined, front legs too long/vertical, hind legs weird.
- Saddle looks like a brown pancake, not a saddle.
- Belly plates are white stripes floating on the front; reference has gray scutes.
- Overall silhouette is a "cartoon bat-lizard", not the reference.

The user is rightly angry. Need to substantially rebuild. We have Blender available for iteration, so we can now render and improve.

Big decision: Could we use aigc_generate_topology to generate a proper dragon model matching the reference, then handle wings? The reference is a single image; image_to_model could produce a good topology dragon in a similar pose. But wings can't flap as a single mesh. The user explicitly asked wings to flap. Could we use the topology model for the body, and animate wings via bone-based deformation? Topology models are single mesh; no rig. Could we segment the mesh in Blender into body/wings and rig? That's complex, and the tool says topology models can't have subparts. Also the workflow doesn't support editing topology mesh. Not allowed to modify topology mesh manually? The skill says topology models only maintain anchor/config/Lua; creating/importing/editing needs model generation. So no.

Maybe generate a topology dragon with wings folded/at sides, then use separate geometry wings that flap? The visual mismatch between topology body and geometry wings would be less bad if the wings are the dominant shape and can be styled similarly. But still complex and risky.

Alternative: substantially improve the geometry model with better shapes. We need a stylized but much closer dragon. We can use custom BufferGeometry lofts for the torso, neck, limbs, tail, and more anatomically shaped wings with 3-4 finger bones and a membrane that arcs. Add head sculpting via custom shapes. We can iterate with Blender renders. This is doable but time-consuming.

Given the user's anger, they want a result close to the reference. Our current model is far off. We need to rebuild rather than tweak. Let's plan a new geometry model with a much better silhouette:

Reference analysis:
- Overall pose: sitting/crouched on hind legs, front legs planted, torso upright and deep-chested, neck long and S-curved rising from the shoulders, head at the top-left, looking slightly down/forward.
- Body: narrow waist relative to chest; chest muscular, deep; belly with horizontal scutes; shoulders broad; hips heavy with folded hind legs.
- Wings: attached at shoulders, huge, swept upward and outward; leading edge arcs high above the head; membrane hangs with 3-4 long finger tips and scalloped trailing edge; the wings frame the body. The wing tips are the highest points. The left wing (viewer's left) is behind the neck, extending up; the right wing extends further right.
- Tail: thick at base, tapers to a thin whip, curves down then strongly up at the tip; large black blade cluster with red inner membrane at the end; small dorsal spikes along the tail.
- Head: narrow elongated snout, angular skull, small amber eye, many swept-back horns/spikes, jaw with teeth, neck with a row of spines.
- Legs: front legs muscular, with defined shoulder and forearm, digitigrade feet with 3 claws; hind legs folded with a big thigh, shin angled back, foot forward.
- Color: near-black scales, slightly lighter gray belly and throat; wing membranes dark with visible bone spars; tail blade black with red interior.

Our model's core issues:
1. Torso is a balloon. Need a lofted body with chest deep and narrow waist, not a pear.
2. Neck too short/stubby. Need 5-6 elongated segments with a graceful S-curve.
3. Wings too small and leaf-like. Need a much larger span (maybe 6m) with long arms and fingers, and membrane shape that arcs.
4. Legs too tubular. Need tapered, jointed limbs with muscle masses at shoulders/thighs and thinner lower legs.
5. Tail too thick and low. Need a longer, tapered tail curving up at the end.
6. Head too chunky. Need a narrower skull, longer snout, swept horns.
7. Saddle looks like a pancake. Make it smaller, darker, and better shaped, or remove it and use a subtle harness? The reference has no saddle. The user's complaint is about matching the reference. A saddle is needed for riding but could be small and unobtrusive. Maybe make a dark leather pad with straps, not a brown pancake. Or use a nearly invisible anchor with a small black harness. Keep a low-profile black saddle so it doesn't dominate.
8. Belly plates are stark white stripes. Make them dark gray, embedded, segmented.
9. Wing spars look like white sticks. Make them dark bone and thinner, positioned along the membrane.
10. Claws are long white needles; make them dark gray and shorter.

Also the model is quite small/cute due to the proportions: body too short, head too big, wings too small. Need to elongate the neck, tail, and wings, narrow the torso, and reduce head size relative to body.

Let's redesign with custom lofts.

Approach for smooth organic volumes:
- Use a `loft` helper that builds a tube along a Catmull-Rom-like centerline with elliptical cross-sections varying in width/height. This can create the torso, neck, tail, limbs, and horns. For the torso, a loft along a curved spine from hips to chest with varying cross-section (wide chest, narrow waist, wide hips). We can also add shoulder and thigh ellipsoids.
- Use `CapsuleGeometry`/tapered cylinders for limbs with joint masses.
- Use custom wing membrane BufferGeometry with 3D curvature, not a flat extruded plane. Use a set of boundary points in 3D and generate a double-sided thick sheet with slight curvature. The membrane can be built as a grid/surface following the wing plane with sag. But a simpler extruded shape placed in a slightly tilted plane could look okay if the outline is right and the finger bones are long.
- Make the wing plane angled: wings sweep upward and slightly backward, with tips high and outward. The reference wings are nearly vertical but with depth. Our current flat wings look like leaves because the arm bones are inside the membrane and the membrane is an outlined leaf. Need the membrane to extend far *behind* the arm bones, with long finger bones radiating from the wrist, creating a bat-wing silhouette. The wing leading edge should have a distinct elbow and wrist, and the membrane spans between 3-4 long fingers, with deep concave scallops at the trailing edge. Our current membrane had a too-small trailing depth and looked leaf-like.
- Make the wings bigger: span ~6m (x ±3.0), height to 4.5m? The reference wingspan relative to body height is roughly 1.3x height. If the dragon is 3.4m tall and the body length 6m, wingspan could be 6m. The rider should sit under the wings; bigger is more epic. But the trigger box and camera need updates. Fine.
- Pose: the reference wings are raised, with tips above the head and the membrane hanging behind. Our wings should also be raised.

Maybe we can aim for a "semi-realistic stylized" dragon. The reference itself is a painted illustration, not photoreal. A smooth stylized model can look good if the silhouette is right.

Let's set new dimensions:
- Overall height (wing tips) ~4.2m, head top ~3.4m, saddle ~2.3m, body length (nose to tail tip) ~8m. That's big. Maybe too big. Rider 0.84m; a dragon mount 4m tall is huge. But the reference is a large dragon. Hmm.
- Current height 3.3m, length 6.1m. The proportions issue is not scale but shape. Keep overall ~3.6m tall, 6.5m long, wingspan 5.5m. That's still large but manageable.

Let's define a new coordinate layout with a more upright torso and long neck:

Ground y=0.
- Hips center: (0, 1.25, -0.9), radius (0.55, 0.62, 0.55).
- Waist: (0, 1.45, -0.25), radius (0.45, 0.58, 0.5).
- Chest: (0, 1.75, 0.35), radius (0.62, 0.68, 0.62).
- Shoulders: (0, 1.85, 0.45), width 1.5.
- Neck base: (0, 2.1, 0.72).
- Neck S-curve: rises and arches forward then back:
  P0 (0,2.10,0.72)
  P1 (0,2.35,0.88)
  P2 (0,2.58,1.05)
  P3 (0,2.85,1.12)
  P4 (0,3.10,1.05)
  P5 (0,3.28,0.88) head base
  The head is at y 3.28, facing forward/down slightly, at z ~1.0-1.5. Head top 3.55.
- Wings: shoulder at (±0.62, 1.95, 0.3). Tips at (±2.75, 4.0, -0.2). Wing leading edge arcs up. Membrane trailing edge extends down to y 2.2 near the body and z -0.8 behind. This frames the body.
- Tail: root (0, 1.2, -1.3), curves down to y 0.5 by z -3, then up to y 1.7 at z -5.0 with the blade. Total length ~4m from root. Overall depth nose 1.8 to tail -5.2 = 7m.
- Front legs: shoulder (±0.55, 1.8, 0.55); elbow (±0.65, 1.15, 0.7); wrist (±0.68, 0.5, 0.82); foot (±0.7, 0.12, 1.0). More muscular upper and thinner lower.
- Hind legs: hip (±0.55, 1.25, -0.95); thigh forward/down to knee (±0.78, 0.7, -0.35); shin down/back to ankle (±0.82, 0.25, -0.9); foot forward (±0.8, 0.12, -0.35). Big thigh mass.
- Saddle: at (0, 2.25, -0.65), small and dark. Seat anchor ~2.4.

Hmm, a 3.55m head height and 4m wing tips. Overall 4.0m tall. Is that too big? The reference dragon is sitting and appears ~3-4x a human height. With player 0.84m, a 3.5m dragon is ~4x. Reasonable.

Camera distance needs to increase to 13, pitch 18.

Trigger size: bbox width 5.5, height 4.0, depth 7.0. Use [6.6, 4.8, 8.4], center around (0, 1.9, -1.5). Relative to anchor (y 2.4, z -0.65): center local (0, -0.5, -0.85).

But before building, let's think about how to make the body look less like balloons:
- Use a lofted torso along the spine with a cross-section that varies. A single continuous mesh from hips to neck base eliminates the segmented balloon look.
- Add pectoral/shoulder muscle masses blended with the chest.
- Add a sagittal crest/spine ridge.
- Use a lofted neck with a smooth taper and an S-curve.
- Use lofted tail with a smooth taper and curve.
- Limbs: use tapered capsules and joint spheres, with thick upper segments and thin lower segments; add shoulder/hip muscle masses.
- Head: build with a lofted skull/snout (a custom shape) or an ellipsoid plus tapered snout, but narrower and longer. Use a wedge-shaped lower jaw.
- Wings: custom membrane shape with a curved leading edge, long finger bones, and deep scallops; tilt the wing plane so it's not a flat leaf from the front.

A loft helper:
```js
function buildLoft(parent, name, material, points, radii, radialSegments=16) {
  // points: array of {p: Vector3, rx, ry} cross-sections along the path
  // Build vertices ring by ring in the XY plane perpendicular to the path direction.
}
```
Simpler: for the torso, use a series of spheres/ellipsoids with heavy overlap; but that's what caused the balloon look. A lofted mesh with smooth shading will look much better. Let's implement a generic "tube along a path with oval cross-sections" generator:

- Input: array of sections: `{ pos: Vector3, radiusX, radiusY, radiusZ? }`? The cross-section plane is perpendicular to the path tangent. For a vertical-ish torso, cross-sections horizontal-ish. For a tail, perpendicular to the tail. We can compute a frame using tangent and a preferred up vector.
- For each section i, compute tangent = normalize(p[i+1]-p[i-1]).
- Build a frame: choose `right = normalize(cross(up, tangent))`, `up2 = cross(tangent, right)`. For a tail with tangent roughly -Z, up=+Y, right = cross(up, tangent) = cross(Y, -Z) = -X? Fine.
- Cross-section: `pos + right*cos(θ)*radiusSide + up2*sin(θ)*radiusUp`.
- Connect rings with quads, add end caps.
- Smooth normals via computeVertexNormals.
This gives organic tubes. Use for torso, neck, tail, limbs, horns.

For the torso, the path is along the spine from tail base to neck base, with cross-sections:

  const contour = outline.map(p => new THREE.Vector2(p[0], p[1]));
  const faces = THREE.ShapeUtils.triangulateShape(contour, []);
  const front = [], back = [];
  outline.forEach(p => {
    front.push(new THREE.Vector3(p[0], p[1], p[2] + thickness/2));
    back.push(new THREE.Vector3(p[0], p[1], p[2] - thickness/2));
  });
  const positions = [];

  // Add back vertices
  back.forEach(v => positions.push(v.x,v.y,v.z));
  const n = outline.length;
  faces.forEach(f => {
    // front

    indices.push(a, d, c);
  }

parts.text:
Much better silhouette but there are still major issues:
1. The wings are asymmetric/malformed: the left wing (viewer left in three-quarter) appears as a thin spike, while the right wing is a large membrane. The membrane shape may have a triangulation/winding problem or the left wing is oriented differently. In the front view, both wings show as large membranes, but in the three-quarter, the left wing looks like a thin sliver because the camera is seeing it edge-on? Wait the reference also shows one wing foreshortened. In the three-quarter view, the dragon faces left; the left wing (behind) is seen edge-on? It looks like a spike extending up-left, not a wing. In the side view, one wing is a big membrane behind, another is a thin spike. This suggests the wing plane is oriented differently than expected: the wings are in the XY plane, so from the side (camera along X), they appear edge-on. From the front (+Z), they appear as big membranes. The reference is a 3/4 view where both wings show membrane area. Our wings are too planar and all in the same plane (vertical), so from the side they vanish. Real bat wings have depth/sweep and a curved surface, and the two wings are angled outward/backward. Need to rotate each wing around Y so it sweeps backward, and maybe around X, giving depth. In the reference, the wings are angled: the left wing extends up-left, the right wing up-right, both with visible membrane from a 3/4 view. The membrane plane is roughly vertical but angled ~30-45° backward. We need to rotate the wing assembly around Y by ±25° so the membrane isn't edge-on from the side.

2. The feet are detached from the legs! The toes/foot meshes are floating on the ground in front of the legs. This is because `buildToes` adds the foot/claws to the `root` group at absolute world positions, but the leg loft geometry is also built at absolute positions within the root. Wait, the leg root is at (0,0,0) and the meshes are built with absolute coordinates, so they should align. But the feet in the render are separate flat blobs on the ground, while the legs end in stumps. Why? The `Foot` ellipsoid is at foot position (0.72,0.13,1.02) with scale (0.18,0.095,0.29) — that's the flat blob. The lower leg ends at wrist (0.70,0.46,0.84). There's a gap from y0.46 to y0.13: the wrist sphere at 0.46 and the foot at 0.13, a 0.33 gap with no connecting ankle. I removed the ankle/pastern. Need to add a short pastern segment from the wrist/ankle down to the foot. Same for hind: ankle at 0.23, foot at 0.13 — a small gap but the foot blob is detached visually. Add a pastern segment and a joint at the foot, and raise the foot to touch.

3. The front legs are still too straight and tubular; the upper arm/forearm are visible, but the feet detached. Fix.

4. The hind legs are okay but the thigh is a big blob; the shin is thin. Reference has folded hind legs with a thick thigh and a more complex shape. Acceptable after foot fix.

5. The tail is long and curves, but the tail tip blade is a tiny red arrow, not the reference's big black scythe. Need a larger, more dramatic blade cluster (black), with red interior. The current blade is too small and red-dominant. Increase to ~0.9m and make the black spikes bigger.

6. The head horns are too long/spiky, like a unicorn/antelope. The reference has shorter, thicker, swept-back horns and many small spikes. Our two long straight horns dominate. Need to shorten and curve them more, make them thicker at the base, and add a crown of smaller spikes. The eyes are too big (cartoonish). Reduce eye size by 30%. The head shape is decent but still a bit horse-like. Add a more pronounced brow and jaw.

7. The neck is too thick and short from the side; it looks like a horse neck. The reference has a slender, S-curved neck. The current neck taper is okay but the base is 0.74 wide, which is thick. Reduce the neck radii by ~15% and lengthen it a bit. The neck currently goes from y1.96 to y3.08; the head at 3.08. The body height is 4.3 with wings. The neck looks short because the chest is high. Maybe lengthen by 0.2 and thin it.

8. The torso is still quite round/blobby, but the loft improved. The belly is a big bulge. Reference has a more streamlined, muscular torso with a defined chest and narrower waist. Our waist is not narrow enough; the belly section at z -0.55 has rx0.58, same as the chest. Need a narrower waist (rx0.44) and a deeper chest. Also the shoulder masses make it look like a gorilla. Reduce and reposition.

9. The wings' membrane is very flat and angular; the trailing edge scallops are shallow and the membrane looks like a kite. Need more depth/sweep, longer finger bones, deeper scallops, and rotate the wings backward. Also the membrane front is uniformly dark gray, while the reference has a black membrane with lighter bone structure. Our finger bones are barely visible (thin). Make the finger bones thicker and lighter (bone color) so they read.

10. The saddle is a brown pancake floating on the back; it looks odd. Make it smaller, darker, and closer to the back. Also the straps are barely visible. Maybe remove the straps and make a low-profile black pad. The reference has no saddle, so less is more.

11. The legs' claws are small and dark; fine.

12. The wing positions: The wing roots at ±0.58, 1.98, 0.34. The left wing in the front view extends up-left, but the membrane's lower part is huge down to y1.1. It looks like a kite. Need to shape it more like the reference: the wing leading edge arches up, the membrane hangs behind with a scalloped trailing edge, and the wing tip is pointed. Our leading edge is straight-ish; add more curve.

13. The body is facing left in the render, but the reference faces left too. Good.

14. The tail is very long and thin; it looks like a rat tail. The reference has a thicker base and a smooth taper, with the blade at the end. Our tail base 0.34, tapering to 0.05 over 4m; it looks thin. Increase the base to 0.4 and keep more thickness through the mid (0.25 at 2m), then taper. Also the tail should curve up more at the end and the blade should be at shoulder height.

15. The back view shows the wings as two big flat panels and the tail. Okay.

The biggest visual problems: detached feet, wing orientation/flatness, tail blade size, head horns/eyes, neck thickness, saddle.

Let's fix these systematically. We can iterate with renders.

First, fix feet:
- Add a pastern/ankle segment connecting the wrist/ankle to the foot center for both front and hind:
  - Front: from wrist (0.70,0.46,0.84) to foot (0.72,0.18,1.00), radius 0.09→0.11; add a joint at the foot top. The foot ellipsoid at y0.13 (center) with ry0.095 → top 0.225, so a pastern ending at y0.18 will connect. Good.
  - Hind: from ankle (0.82,0.23,-0.88) to foot (0.82,0.16,-0.42), radius 0.10→0.13. Wait the foot is at z -0.42, forward of the ankle (-0.88). A pastern from the ankle forward/down to the foot. Add. The foot center y0.13, top 0.235. Good.
- Also add a heel/ankle sphere at the foot top.

Why did the feet appear so far in front? The front foot at z1.02 and the leg lower end at z0.84; the foot extends forward 0.29, plus toes to z1.4. The visual gap is mostly vertical. Add the pastern.

Second, fix wings:
- Rotate each wing root around Y: left wing should sweep back (local -Z) as it extends outward. If we rotate the wing root around Y by +25° for the left (glTF +X side), the wing plane rotates: x→? Rotation about Y by +θ maps +X toward -Z? In Three.js, rotation Y positive: x' = x cos + z sin; z' = -x sin + z cos. For a point at +X, z' = -x sin → negative z (back). Good. So rotate the left wing root Y +25°; for the right wing at -X, rotate Y -25° to sweep back. In Unity, the Y rotation sign flips, but the initial rotation is baked in the model; Lua only sets Z. Fine.
- Also tilt the wing plane outward? Maybe rotate X slightly (-5°) to angle the membrane. The Y sweep will give depth.
- Increase the membrane's trailing edge depth and scallops. The current membrane is a big triangle. Add deeper scallops and a more curved leading edge.
- Make the finger bones thicker and lighter (bone color). Add a leading-edge arm that is more curved.
- The wing tip should extend higher and further out: currently 2.45x, 2.25y. The model height 4.3. Maybe fine. The reference wings are huge; ours are large. With the Y rotation, the width will reduce (x*cos) and depth increase. Wingspan becomes 2.45*cos25*2 + 1.16 = 5.6, still large.
- The wing membranes from the front will be angled, showing more area. Good.

Third, tail:
- Increase the base radius to 0.42 and mid radii; make the tail thicker and shorter? The reference tail is long but tapered. Keep length 4.0, but thicker:
  0.42, 0.36, 0.30, 0.245, 0.195, 0.15, 0.11, 0.08, 0.055.
- The tail tip currently at y0.48 local + root 1.08 = 1.56; the blade top ~2.2. The reference tail tip is high (near the shoulders ~2.0). Raise the tip to y1.1 local (world 2.18) by adjusting the last sections: (0,0.55,-3.74), (0,0.95,-4.05), and add another section (0,1.35,-4.25) maybe. This will make the tail arc up more. But the total length increases. Use 9 sections ending at (0,1.0,-4.15). The blade at the tip.
- Make the blade 1.5x bigger and mostly black with red inner. The current blade group at (0,0.48,-4.05) with blades 0.58 long; scale up to 0.9 and darker. Add a big central curved blade and two side blades. The red fin should be smaller relative to the black blades.
- The tail spikes are tiny; make them bigger (0.25 tall) and more numerous.

Fourth, head:

parts.text:
Now much better. The feet are connected, the wings have depth, the tail is long and curls up with a blade. But compared to the reference:

1. The wings are still not big enough / not shaped like the reference. In the three-quarter view, the near wing is a large kite; the far wing is a thin sliver (because it's edge-on). The reference has both wings visible. The wing sweep angle should be more outward and less backward? Actually the reference is a 3/4 view with both wings visible, but one is partly behind the neck. Our far wing is nearly invisible because the sweep is 24°; from this camera angle, it's edge-on. Maybe rotate the camera? But the user will view from arbitrary angles. A wing is a thin membrane; from some angles it will be edge-on. That's natural. The reference's far wing is also somewhat foreshortened but visible. Our far wing is too thin because the membrane is nearly planar and the camera is aligned with its plane. If we add more curvature/cupping, it will catch light from more angles. Also, in the render, the near wing looks like a big flat kite with a straight leading edge. The reference wing has a graceful curved leading edge and a more complex membrane. Need to improve the wing shape.

2. The body is still somewhat lumpy: the shoulders/hips are distinct balls, the belly is a big bulge, the front legs are thin sticks. The reference has a muscular torso and legs. Our front legs are too thin and straight; the hind legs are better but still simple. The body's waist is narrow now, but the chest is still a round ball. The reference has a broad, muscular chest and a more upright torso.

3. The neck is still a bit thick and straight from the side; the reference has a more graceful S-curve. Ours is okay.

4. The head is better (shorter horns), but the face is still horse-like. The reference has a more angular, reptilian head with a pronounced brow and a longer snout. Ours has a rounded muzzle. Add a more angular jaw, a brow ridge, and maybe a nose horn. The eyes are better.

5. The tail blade is still red-dominant and looks like a red arrow; the reference has a black blade cluster with red inner membrane. Our black spikes are thin and the red fin dominates. Make the black blades much thicker/larger and the red fin smaller. Also the tail tip is high, good.

6. The saddle is now small and dark, barely visible. Good.

7. The tail is thick at the base, good. It looks like a long tail. The spikes are tiny; make them a bit larger.

8. The wings' membrane is a uniform flat gray, and the finger bones are barely visible. Need more visible bones, perhaps lighter gray and thicker. The reference's wing membrane is black with visible bone structure. Our membrane is dark and the bones are dark; low contrast. Make the bones lighter (0x5a564c) and thicker.

9. The feet are now connected but the front legs look like thin sticks with big feet. Make the upper arms thicker and the lower arms slightly thicker. The reference has muscular forelimbs.

10. The overall silhouette is now closer, but the body is still short/compact compared to the reference's elongated, upright body. The reference's torso is longer and more vertical; ours is a horizontal egg. Need to elongate the torso and raise the chest. The neck base is at z0.92; the chest is round. The reference's chest is deep and broad, with the neck rising from the top. Our chest at y1.83, z0.72, radius 0.58/0.62; the body is 1.7m long. The reference's torso looks ~2m long and more vertical. Hmm.

Maybe we should increase the torso's vertical extent: raise the chest to y2.0 and lower the hips to y1.15, creating a more upright chest. The current spine goes from y1.16 at the hips to y1.98 at the neck base, a rise of 0.82 over 2.24 z. The reference's spine is more like 45°, rise ~1.2 over 1.5. We could raise the chest by 0.15 and move it back 0.1. But this would require moving the neck, wings, front legs, saddle, and scutes. A lot of edits with risk.

Alternatively, keep the current pose; it's a credible sitting dragon. The user's main complaint was likely the cartoon bat look; the new model is much closer. But they said "你自己看看你跟参考图的关系" — they expect a close match. Our new model still looks like a stylized low-poly dragon, not the reference's detailed art. Geometry modeling has limits. Maybe the best approach is to use the AIGC topology model for the body and accept that wings can't flap? But the user explicitly wants flapping. Hmm.

Could we generate a topology model of the dragon in the reference pose with wings, then use Blender to split the wing geometry from the mesh and rig it for flapping? The instruction says topology models are complete mesh and don't support subparts, but we could use Blender to deform? The tool's export pipeline expects one GLB; we could import the topology GLB into Blender, cut the wings, add armatures, and export a new GLB. But the skill says topology models only maintain anchor/config/Lua, and creating/importing/editing topology requires model generation; manual mesh editing is not supported. Also, the archive expects static/preview-module.js for geometry or topology/model.glb. If we modify the topology GLB externally, that's likely against the workflow. Not allowed.

Another option: use AIGC to generate the dragon with wings in a *flapping pose*, then use a shape key? No.

So geometry is the route. We can continue refining.

The biggest visual mismatch now is the wings' shape and the body/limb refinement. Let's focus on the wings and overall silhouette.

Reference wing analysis:
- The wings are enormous, with the leading edge rising almost vertically from the shoulders, then angling outward. The wing tips are above the head and spread wide.
- The membrane hangs from long finger bones that radiate from the wrist, creating a scalloped trailing edge with 4-5 points.
- The wing surface is not a flat kite; it curves.
- The far wing is partly hidden behind the neck but still visible as a large shape.

Our wings: the leading edge starts at the shoulder, goes to the elbow (0.82,0.88), wrist (1.56,1.72), tip (2.45,2.25). The membrane trailing edge sweeps to y-0.75 near the body. From the front, it looks like a big triangular kite with a straight leading edge. The finger bones are visible but thin. We could:
- Make the leading edge more curved: elbow at (0.55,1.05), wrist (1.15,1.95), tip (2.35,2.55). This raises the wing higher, matching the reference.
- Add a second "thumb claw" at the wrist, pointing up.
- Make the trailing edge scallops deeper and more numerous (4 fingers). The membrane should have a pronounced concave curve between fingers.
- Add curvature in Z: the membrane's trailing edge should billow backward (negative z) and the middle should sag. Our z values already vary, but the sweep makes it look flat. Add a slight bulge by moving the finger tips further back and the valleys forward.
- Rotate the wing plane outward (around the local Y) less? Our sweep 24° makes the far wing edge-on from the 3/4 camera. The reference wings are roughly in the frontal plane, so a 3/4 view shows both. Maybe reduce the sweep to 12° and add a slight outward cant (rotate around X?) to give depth. Or keep 20°.

In the reference, the wings are seen from a 3/4 angle and both are visible, so the wing planes are roughly frontal with some backward sweep. Use 15°.

- Increase the wing size: tip y 2.6, x 2.8. The overall height 4.6. The model already 4.3; a bit bigger. The reference wings are huge relative to the body. Our wings are about 2.2m tall from the shoulder, the body height ~2.4. The reference wings are ~1.5x the body height. Our wing tip y 4.3 vs body 2.2 → 2x. Fine.

Our near wing in the three-quarter looks like a flat kite because the membrane is a single triangulated polygon with a straight leading edge. Add an elbow bend and a wrist, with the leading edge curving. Make the membrane attach along the body and hang lower.

Also, the wing membrane's surface currently has no interior vertices, so it's a flat polygon between the boundary points. The z variation at the boundary creates a twisted surface, but the interior is a flat triangulation. To make it look curved, add interior vertices. We could subdivide the membrane into a grid and displace z based on x/y. That's more work but doable:
- Instead of a polygon triangulation, build the membrane as a parametric surface between the leading edge and trailing edge. For each u along the span (0..1) and v across the chord (0..1), define points by interpolating between the leading edge curve L(u) and trailing edge curve T(u), with a billow offset in z. This creates a smooth curved sheet. But the trailing edge is scalloped, which is a function of u. We can define L(u) and T(u) piecewise. The membrane would be a grid with thickness. This is a better approach.
- However, the outline is complex. A grid surface can be built from the leading edge to the trailing edge with 16 span segments and 8 chord segments. The trailing edge is defined by the scalloped outline; we can interpolate between the finger tips and valleys. Then add thickness. This would look much smoother and more organic.

Maybe simpler: keep the polygon but add a slight inward billow by moving the interior? Not possible without interior vertices. Could triangulate and then subdivide each triangle, displacing z. Complex.

Alternatively, use a `ParametricGeometry`-like grid. Let's implement a wing surface generator:
- Define leading edge samples L(t) for t=0..1 along the arm from shoulder→tip.
- Define trailing edge samples T(t) for t=0..1 from the body attachment→tip, with scallops. Actually at each span fraction t, the trailing edge point is a curve from the body to the tip. We can define T(t) by interpolating the finger valleys? Hmm.
- A bat wing membrane is bounded by the leading edge (arm+finger1) and the trailing edge (scallops between fingers). It's a single surface. A grid from the leading edge to the trailing edge with t along the span works: for each t, the leading edge point is on the arm, and the trailing edge point is on the scalloped edge. But the trailing edge has multiple lobes; the mapping along t is not trivial. We can define T(t) as a piecewise curve through the trailing points. Interpolating between the boundary points by arc length. Then the grid fills between L(t) and T(t). This would produce a smooth surface with scallops.
- Build vertices for t=0..1, s=0..1: P(t,s) = lerp(L(t), T(t), s) + billow(t,s) in z (negative/back). Add thickness. The surface will have a nice curved billow.

parts.text:
The model is still clearly a stylized dragon, but closer to the reference. However, the user is angry and wants a strong resemblance. We need to decide whether to keep iterating or acknowledge the limits. Let's compare to the reference:

- Reference: dragon facing left, wings raised, one wing behind the neck extending left, the other wing up-right, membrane with multiple long fingers and scalloped edges. Our 3/4 view: only one wing is fully visible (right side); the left wing is a thin vertical sliver behind the head. This is the biggest remaining mismatch. Why? The wing plane is perpendicular to the camera for the far wing. In the reference, both wings are visible. Our far wing's membrane is edge-on because the wing root is at the shoulder and the wing plane is nearly vertical, and the camera is at ~40°; the far wing's plane normal is roughly 40° away, so it should show some area, but the render shows a thin sliver. Wait, in the 3/4 image, the far wing (left side) is a thin vertical strip with a small triangle at the top left. That suggests the far wing's membrane is nearly edge-on. The camera is at (11,-13.5,6.8) looking at the center; the view direction has x and y components. The far wing plane (after sweep 12.6°) has a normal roughly (sin(sweep), 0, cos?) Let's compute. The wing plane is initially XY with normal +Z. A Y rotation by +12.6° rotates the normal to (sin12.6, 0, cos12.6) = (0.218, 0, 0.976). The camera direction from the model to the camera is (11, -13.5, 6.8) normalized, but in Blender coordinates; the model front is -Y. The camera is to the right (+X) and front (-Y). This is now a reasonably recognizable black western dragon with big bat wings, long neck, tail with blade. Still stylized, not the painted reference. But much better than the first. Camera distance: The model is 5.95 wide, 4.64 tall, 7.96 long. The rider seat at 2.205. Camera distance 14, pitch 18, offset 2.4. Is 14 enough to see the whole dragon? The chase camera is behind the player; the dragon is 8m long, so the tail extends 5.8m behind the seat. The camera at 14m behind the player (seat) is 8m behind the tail; the dragon fits. input.content:
-- 黑龙鞍座：靠近触发、上下座按钮、骑手对齐与离座恢复
---@displayName 黑龙鞍座
---@start
---@var TriggerRangeScale:number=1
---@name 触发范围倍率
---@desc 基于初始触发范围等比放大
---@group 交互
---@end

local UnityEngine = CS.UnityEngine
local RuntimeScope = require("official.core.runtime_scope")
local Trigger = require("official.interaction.trigger")

local runtimeScope = RuntimeScope.from(self)
local TriggerRangeScaleApplied = Trigger.applyRangeScale(self, TriggerRangeScale)

local interactionButton = nil
local localActorId = nil
local hasLocalPassenger = false
local localActor = nil

local seatedActors = {}
local savedScale = {}
local savedPosition = {}
local savedRotation = {}
local savedColliderEnabled = {}

local flightScript = nil

local function getFlightScript()
  if flightScript ~= nil then return flightScript end
  if runtimeScope == nil then return nil end
  flightScript = runtimeScope:GetScript("ms-flight.lua")
  return flightScript
end

local function notifyFlight(active)
  local flight = getFlightScript()
  if flight == nil or type(flight.SetRiderActive) ~= "function" then return end
  flight.SetRiderActive(active)
end

local function setButtonText(text)
  if interactionButton == nil then return end
  local label = interactionButton:GetComponentInChildren(
    typeof(CS.UnityEngine.UI.Text), true)
  if label ~= nil then
    label.text = text
  end
end

local function ensureInteractionButton()
  if interactionButton == nil then
    interactionButton = self:AddInteractorButton()
  end
  setButtonText(hasLocalPassenger and "站起" or "坐下")
end

local function removeInteractionButton()
  if interactionButton ~= nil then
    self:RemoveInteractorButton(interactionButton)
    interactionButton = nil
  end
end

local function resolveSeatTrans()
  return self.transform
end

local function alignActorHipsToSeat(actor, target)
  target = target or resolveSeatTrans()
  if actor == nil or actor.gameObject == nil or target == nil then return end

  local trans = actor.gameObject.transform
  trans:SetParent(target)
  trans.localPosition = UnityEngine.Vector3.zero
  trans.localRotation = UnityEngine.Quaternion.identity

  local original = savedScale[actor] or UnityEngine.Vector3.one
  local parentScale = target.lossyScale
  trans.localScale = UnityEngine.Vector3(
    original.x / (parentScale.x ~= 0 and parentScale.x or 1),
    original.y / (parentScale.y ~= 0 and parentScale.y or 1),
    original.z / (parentScale.z ~= 0 and parentScale.z or 1)
  )

  local animator = actor.gameObject:GetComponentInChildren(
    typeof(CS.UnityEngine.Animator))
  if animator == nil then return end

  local hips = animator:GetBoneTransform(CS.UnityEngine.HumanBodyBones.Hips)
  if hips == nil then return end

  local hipsPosition = hips.position
  local actorPosition = trans.position
  trans.position = UnityEngine.Vector3(
    actorPosition.x - (hipsPosition.x - actorPosition.x),
    actorPosition.y - (hipsPosition.y - actorPosition.y),
    actorPosition.z - (hipsPosition.z - actorPosition.z)
  )
end

local function setActorColliderEnabled(actor, enabled)
  if actor == nil or actor.gameObject == nil then return end
  local collider = actor.gameObject:GetComponent(typeof(CS.UnityEngine.Collider))
  if collider == nil then return end

  if not enabled then
    savedColliderEnabled[actor] = collider.enabled
    collider.enabled = false
  else
    local previous = savedColliderEnabled[actor]
    collider.enabled = previous == nil or previous
    savedColliderEnabled[actor] = nil
  end
end

local function placeActorAtStandPoint(actor)
  if actor == nil or actor.gameObject == nil then return end

  local trans = actor.gameObject.transform
  trans:SetParent(nil)

  if savedScale[actor] ~= nil then
    trans.localScale = savedScale[actor]
    savedScale[actor] = nil
  end

  local savedPos = savedPosition[actor]
  local savedRot = savedRotation[actor]
  if savedPos ~= nil and savedRot ~= nil then
    actor.position = savedPos
    actor.rotation = savedRot
  else
    local right = self.transform.right
    local base = self.transform.position
    actor.position = UnityEngine.Vector3(
      base.x + right.x * 1.2,
      base.y,
      base.z + right.z * 1.2
    )
    actor.rotation = self.transform.rotation
  end

  savedPosition[actor] = nil
  savedRotation[actor] = nil
end

function OnActorTriggerEnter(actor)
  if actor == nil or not actor.isLocal then return end
  localActorId = actor.actorID
  self:EnableInteraction()
end

function OnActorTriggerExit(actor)
  if actor == nil or not actor.isLocal then return end

  -- 在座时保留 Actor ID 和交互通道，保证飞行中仍能站起。
  if not hasLocalPassenger then
    self:DisableInteraction()
    localActorId = nil
  end
end

function OnFocus(handType)
  ensureInteractionButton()
end

function OnLostFocus(handType)
  removeInteractionButton()
end

function OnInteractorButtonClick(index)
  if index ~= 1 or localActorId == nil then return end

  local actor = DouyinActorService.GetActorById(localActorId)
  if actor == nil then return end

  if hasLocalPassenger then
    actor:StandUp(self.gameObject)
  else
    if actor:IsFlying() or resolveSeatTrans() == nil then return end
    actor:SitDown(self.gameObject, true)
  end
end

function OnSeatEntered(actor, handType)
  if actor == nil or actor.gameObject == nil then return end

  local target = resolveSeatTrans()
  if target == nil then return end

  local trans = actor.gameObject.transform
  savedPosition[actor] = trans.position
  savedRotation[actor] = trans.rotation
  savedScale[actor] = trans.localScale

  alignActorHipsToSeat(actor, target)
  seatedActors[actor] = target
  setActorColliderEnabled(actor, false)

  if actor.isLocal then
    hasLocalPassenger = true
    localActor = actor
    if actor.Immobilize ~= nil then
      actor:Immobilize(true)
    end
    self:EnableInteraction()
    ensureInteractionButton()
    notifyFlight(true)
  end
end

function OnSeatExited(actor)
  if actor == nil or actor.gameObject == nil then return end

  -- 先停止持续对齐，再解除挂载，避免离座后又被拉回座位。
  seatedActors[actor] = nil
  placeActorAtStandPoint(actor)
  setActorColliderEnabled(actor, true)

  if actor.isLocal then
    hasLocalPassenger = false
    if localActor == actor then
      localActor = nil
    end
    if actor.Immobilize ~= nil then
      actor:Immobilize(false)
    end
    setButtonText("坐下")
    notifyFlight(false)
  end
end

function LateUpdate()
  for actor, target in pairs(seatedActors) do
    alignActorHipsToSeat(actor, target)
  end
end

local function cleanupLocalRider()
  if localActor ~= nil and localActor.Immobilize ~= nil then
    localActor:Immobilize(false)
  end
  localActor = nil
  hasLocalPassenger = false
  seatedActors = {}
  notifyFlight(false)
end

function OnDisable()
  removeInteractionButton()
end

function OnDestroy()
  removeInteractionButton()
  cleanupLocalRider()
end

---@desc 未被骑乘时每秒轻扇翅膀的次数
---@group 表现
---@end

local UnityEngine = CS.UnityEngine
local Vector2 = CS.UnityEngine.Vector2
local Vector3 = CS.UnityEngine.Vector3
local Quaternion = CS.UnityEngine.Quaternion
local Mathf = CS.UnityEngine.Mathf
local Time = CS.UnityEngine.Time
local Input = CS.UnityEngine.Input
local KeyCode = CS.UnityEngine.KeyCode
local DouyinInputService = CS.DouyinInputService
local DouyinUIService = CS.DouyinUIService
local UIType = CS.UIType
local EventTrigger = CS.UnityEngine.EventSystems.EventTrigger
local EventTriggerType = CS.UnityEngine.EventSystems.EventTriggerType
local RuntimeScope = require("official.core.runtime_scope")

local runtimeScope = RuntimeScope.from(self)

local deadZone = 0.12
local idleDamping = 4.5
local horizontalAccel = 9
local verticalAccel = 7
local pitchAngle = 18
local rollAngle = 20
local motionLerpSpeed = 5
local flightFlapAmplitude = 30
local idleFlapAmplitude = 8
local bobAmplitude = 0.035

local rb = nil
local visualRoot = nil
local wingLeft = nil
local wingRight = nil
local neckRoot = nil
local tailNodes = {}
local tailBaseX = {-10.3, -6.9, -3.4, 1.1, 8.0, 14.9, 21.8, 26.4}

local moveVec = Vector2.zero
local onMoveInputStart = nil
local onMoveInputPerform = nil
local onMoveInputCancel = nil

local riderActive = false
local controlReady = false
local controlSupported = false
local controlPending = false
local nextControlTry = 0
local velocityX = 0
local velocityY = 0
local velocityZ = 0
local m_yaw = 0
local m_pitch = 0
local m_roll = 0
local animationTime = 0
local rideCameraApplied = false

local ascendBtn = nil
local ascendTrigger = nil
local descendBtn = nil
local descendTrigger = nil
local btnAscend = false
local btnDescend = false

local function clearTrigger(trigger)
  if trigger == nil then return end
  if trigger.triggers ~= nil then
    trigger.triggers:Clear()
  end
end

local function bindTrigger(btn, onDown, onUp)
  if btn == nil or btn.gameObject == nil then return nil end
  local trigger = btn.gameObject:GetComponent(typeof(EventTrigger))
  if trigger == nil then
    trigger = btn.gameObject:AddComponent(typeof(EventTrigger))
  end
  clearTrigger(trigger)

  local entryDown = EventTrigger.Entry()
  entryDown.eventID = EventTriggerType.PointerDown
  entryDown.callback:AddListener(function(_) onDown() end)
  trigger.triggers:Add(entryDown)

  local entryUp = EventTrigger.Entry()
  entryUp.eventID = EventTriggerType.PointerUp
  entryUp.callback:AddListener(function(_) onUp() end)
  trigger.triggers:Add(entryUp)

  return trigger
end

local function setButtonText(btn, text)
  if btn == nil then return end
  local label = btn:GetComponentInChildren(typeof(CS.UnityEngine.UI.Text), true)
  if label ~= nil then
    label.gameObject:SetActive(true)
    label.text = text
  end
end

local function setupActionButton(uiType, btnText, onDown, onUp)
  local btn = DouyinUIService.GetInteractionButton(uiType)
  if btn == nil then return nil, nil end
  btn.gameObject:SetActive(true)
  btn.transition = CS.UnityEngine.UI.Selectable.Transition.None
  local tween = btn.gameObject:GetComponentInChildren(typeof(CS.ButtonTweenEffect), true)
  if tween ~= nil then
    tween.enabled = false
  end
  setButtonText(btn, btnText)
  local trigger = bindTrigger(btn, onDown, onUp)
  return btn, trigger
end

local function hideButton(btn, trigger)
  if trigger ~= nil then clearTrigger(trigger) end
  if btn ~= nil then btn.gameObject:SetActive(false) end
end

local function showFlightButtons()
  if ascendBtn ~= nil or descendBtn ~= nil then return end
  ascendBtn, ascendTrigger = setupActionButton(
    UIType.CustomMain, "上升",
    function() if riderActive then btnAscend = true end end,
    function() btnAscend = false end
  )
  descendBtn, descendTrigger = setupActionButton(
    UIType.CustomSub, "下降",
    function() if riderActive then btnDescend = true end end,
    function() btnDescend = false end
  )
end

local function hideFlightButtons()
  hideButton(ascendBtn, ascendTrigger)
  ascendBtn = nil
  ascendTrigger = nil
  hideButton(descendBtn, descendTrigger)
  descendBtn = nil
  descendTrigger = nil
  btnAscend = false
  btnDescend = false
end

local function applyRideCamera()
  if rideCameraApplied then return end
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetDistance(11)
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetPitch(16)
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetOffset(Vector3(0, 1.9, 0))
  rideCameraApplied = true
end

local function restoreRideCamera()
  if not rideCameraApplied then return end
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetDistance(4)
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetPitch(0)
  CS.DouyinCameraService.SetOffset(Vector3(0, 0, 0))
  rideCameraApplied = false
end

local function clearInput()
  moveVec = Vector2.zero
  btnAscend = false
  btnDescend = false
  velocityX = 0
  velocityY = 0
  velocityZ = 0
end

local function requestControl()
  if not controlSupported or controlPending or controlReady then return end
  if self:IsNull() then return end
  if self:HasControllership() then
    controlReady = true
    return
  end

  controlPending = true
  self:RequestControllership(function(success)
    controlPending = false
    if self:IsNull() then return end
    if success and self:HasControllership() then
      controlReady = true
    else
      nextControlTry = Time.time + 1.0
    end
  end)
end

local function releaseControl()
  controlReady = false
  if controlSupported and self:HasControllership() then
    self:ReleaseControllership()
  end
end

local function resolveVerticalInput()
  local up = Input.GetKey(KeyCode.E) or btnAscend
  local down = Input.GetKey(KeyCode.Q) or btnDescend
  if up and not down then return 1 end
  if down and not up then return -1 end
  return 0
end

local function findNodes()
  if runtimeScope == nil then return end
  visualRoot = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot")
  wingLeft = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot/WingLeftRoot")
  wingRight = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot/WingRightRoot")
  neckRoot = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot/NeckRoot")

  tailNodes[1] = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath("DragonRoot/VisualRoot/TailRoot")
  local path = "DragonRoot/VisualRoot/TailRoot"
  for index = 1, 7 do
    path = path .. string.format("/Tail%02d", index)
    tailNodes[index + 1] = runtimeScope:GetTransformByPath(path)
  end
end

local function animateCreature()
  animationTime = animationTime + Time.deltaTime
  local flying = riderActive and controlReady
  local flapHz = flying and FlightFlapSpeed or IdleFlapSpeed
  local flapAmplitude = flying and flightFlapAmplitude or idleFlapAmplitude
  local flap = Mathf.Sin(animationTime * flapHz * 2 * Mathf.PI) * flapAmplitude

  -- Unity 的 X 轴相对 glTF 镜像：左翼位于 -X，需要反向 Z 旋转抬翼。
  if wingLeft ~= nil then
    wingLeft.localEulerAngles = Vector3(0, 0, -flap)
  end
  if wingRight ~= nil then
    wingRight.localEulerAngles = Vector3(0, 0, flap)
  end

  local swayAmplitude = flying and 5.0 or 2.5
  for index = 1, #tailNodes do
    local node = tailNodes[index]
    if node ~= nil then
      local sway = Mathf.Sin(animationTime * 1.25 - index * 0.42) * swayAmplitude
      node.localEulerAngles = Vector3(tailBaseX[index], sway, 0)
    end
  end

  if neckRoot ~= nil then
    local neckBob = Mathf.Sin(animationTime * 0.85) * 1.2
    neckRoot.localEulerAngles = Vector3(neckBob, 0, 0)
  end

  if visualRoot ~= nil then
    local bob = 0
    if flying then
      bob = Mathf.Sin(animationTime * 2.1) * bobAmplitude
    end
    visualRoot.localPosition = Vector3(0, bob, 0)
  end
end

function Start()
  rb = self.gameObject:GetComponent(typeof(UnityEngine.Rigidbody))
  controlSupported = self.HasControllership ~= nil and self.RequestControllership ~= nil
  findNodes()

  onMoveInputStart = function()
    -- 起手时保持当前方向，由 Perform 覆盖。
  end
  onMoveInputPerform = function(vec)
    moveVec = vec
  end
  onMoveInputCancel = function()
    moveVec = Vector2.zero
  end

  DouyinInputService.onMoveInputStart:AddListener(onMoveInputStart)
  DouyinInputService.onMoveInputPerform:AddListener(onMoveInputPerform)
  DouyinInputService.onMoveInputCancel:AddListener(onMoveInputCancel)
end

function SetRiderActive(active)
  if active then
    if riderActive then return end
    riderActive = true
    velocityX = 0
    velocityY = 0
    velocityZ = 0
    m_pitch = 0
    m_roll = 0
    m_yaw = self.transform.eulerAngles.y
    controlReady = not controlSupported
    nextControlTry = 0
    applyRideCamera()
    showFlightButtons()
    if controlSupported then
      requestControl()
    end
  else
    if not riderActive then return end
    riderActive = false
    clearInput()
    m_pitch = 0
    m_roll = 0
    hideFlightButtons()
    restoreRideCamera()
    releaseControl()
  end
end

function OnControllershipTransferred(prevPlayer, currentPlayer)
  if not controlSupported then return end
  controlReady = self:HasControllership()
  if not controlReady and riderActive then
    nextControlTry = Time.time + 1.0
  end
end

function Update()
  animateCreature()

  if riderActive and controlSupported and not controlReady and not controlPending
    and Time.time >= nextControlTry then
    requestControl()
  end
end

function FixedUpdate()
  if not riderActive or not controlReady or rb == nil then return end

  local dt = Time.fixedDeltaTime
  local forwardInput = moveVec.y
  local turnInput = moveVec.x
  if math.abs(forwardInput) < deadZone then forwardInput = 0 end
  if math.abs(turnInput) < deadZone then turnInput = 0 end
  local verticalInput = resolveVerticalInput()

  m_yaw = m_yaw + turnInput * TurnSpeed * dt
  local targetPitch = -verticalInput * pitchAngle
  local targetRoll = -turnInput * rollAngle
  local lerpT = Mathf.Clamp01(motionLerpSpeed * dt)
  m_pitch = Mathf.Lerp(m_pitch, targetPitch, lerpT)
  m_roll = Mathf.Lerp(m_roll, targetRoll, lerpT)
  rb:MoveRotation(Quaternion.Euler(m_pitch, m_yaw, m_roll))

  local forward = self.transform.forward
  local horizontalForward = Vector3(forward.x, 0, forward.z)
  if horizontalForward.sqrMagnitude <= 0.0001 then
    horizontalForward = Vector3(0, 0, 1)
  else
    horizontalForward:Normalize()
  end

  local targetX = horizontalForward.x * forwardInput * HorizontalSpeed
  local targetZ = horizontalForward.z * forwardInput * HorizontalSpeed
  local targetY = verticalInput * VerticalSpeed
  local horizontalStep = (forwardInput == 0 and idleDamping or horizontalAccel) * dt
  local verticalStep = (verticalInput == 0 and idleDamping or verticalAccel) * dt

  velocityX = Mathf.MoveTowards(velocityX, targetX, horizontalStep)
  velocityZ = Mathf.MoveTowards(velocityZ, targetZ, horizontalStep)
  velocityY = Mathf.MoveTowards(velocityY, targetY, verticalStep)

  local nextPosition = rb.position + Vector3(velocityX, velocityY, velocityZ) * dt
  rb:MovePosition(nextPosition)
end

function OnDisable()
  if riderActive then
    riderActive = false
    clearInput()
    hideFlightButtons()
    restoreRideCamera()
    releaseControl()
  end
end

function OnDestroy()
  if onMoveInputStart ~= nil then
    DouyinInputService.onMoveInputStart:RemoveListener(onMoveInputStart)
    onMoveInputStart = nil
  end
  if onMoveInputPerform ~= nil then
    DouyinInputService.onMoveInputPerform:RemoveListener(onMoveInputPerform)
    onMoveInputPerform = nil
  end
  if onMoveInputCancel ~= nil then
    DouyinInputService.onMoveInputCancel:RemoveListener(onMoveInputCancel)
    onMoveInputCancel = nil
  end
  hideFlightButtons()
  restoreRideCamera()
  releaseControl()
end
